chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Usury (riba) is two types: a usury that is eaten and a usury that is not eaten.
As for that which is eaten, it is your gift to a man, seeking from him a reward greater than it; that is the usury which is eaten.
And it is His Word, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And whatever you give as usury, so that it may increase in the property of the people, it will not increase in the Presence of Allah.'
And as for that which is not eaten, it is the usury which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, forbade and promised the Fire for.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the two types of usury (riba) according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between two types of usury (riba): one that is 'eaten' (consumed/lost spiritually), which refers to a gift given with the expectation of a greater return, and one that is 'not eaten', which is the specific usury forbidden by Allah and punished with Hellfire. The text cites Quran 30:39 to support the concept of riba that does not increase with God. This classification highlights the subtle distinction between social reciprocity that becomes exploitative and the formal interest-based transactions condemned in Sharia.
